AUTHOR: Varini
TITLE: SharkTrack: An accurate, generalisable software for streamlining shark and ray underwater video analysis
REGION: Training: BRUVS from 25 locations worldwide (incl. Global FinPrint); test: Red Sea (Saudi Arabia), Anguilla (Caribbean), North Male Atoll (Maldives)
SPECIES: Elasmobranchs (sharks and rays) merged into a single 'elasmobranch' detection class; test sets contain 15 (Red Sea), 5 (Anguilla), 7 (Maldives) species, e.g., nurse sharks, grey reef shark; species assigned manually
DATA: Own/partner BRUVS: 77 video snippets (~2 h) from 25 locations, 1 fps, plus 587 Batoidea instances from Open Images (social media); final 7,049 annotated images. Test: 207 h BRUVS footage from 3 unseen locations (Red Sea, Anguilla, Maldives) with manual ssMaxN
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'Videos collected in the Red Sea presented rocky reef habitats with clear water. Visibility was more than 5 m in most videos'; Sec. 3.2: 'In this turbid water ... SharkTrack achieved an accuracy of 87.8%'
D2: Train/val random 85:15 split on locations (25 locations); separate test set of 207 h BRUVS from 3 locations not in training
D_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'using a random 85:15 split on locations rather than images, to ensure full independence between images from the training and validation set'
R_EV: Sec. 2.1: 'we collected a test dataset of 207 h of BRUVS footage from three locations not represented in the training data'; in-domain reported only as mAP50 0.85, external only as MaxN Accuracy
C_EV: Sec. 4: 'the average false positive rate was 86% (estimated by manually verifying 100 randomly sampled detections per location'; Sec. 2.2: 'confidence threshold of 0.2'
E_EV: Sec. 3: 'We compared the ground truth ssMaxN, computed manually, with the ssMaxN computed by analysts using the SharkTrack semi-automatic process'; Table 1 MaxN Accuracy 81.8/87.8/97.8%
ARCH: YOLOv8-nano single-class elasmobranch detector (640 px, 500 epochs, batch 64, conf 0.2) + BotSORT MOT with tuned post-processing + human-in-the-loop species classification and FP deletion, ssMaxN computation
METR: mAP50 (validation, 0.85); precision/recall/F1 in SI S2; per-species MaxN Accuracy averaged per video; ML inference time and manual post-processing time vs traditional manual analysis time; false-positive rate from 100 sampled detections per location
NOTE: Elasmobranchs treated as fish (cf. S055). Detector is single-class; species ID is manual, so TAXA reflects species covered by pipeline output (27 species across test sets, overlapping), verifier may prefer 과/속 수준. V1 = 기타 정량 based on 'visibility more than 5 m' for Red Sea own footage (S107 precedent); Caribbean turbidity only qualitative; per-location performance with eye-assessed water conditions -> V6 = P. D1 coded 지역 (split on locations; test = 3 unseen regions). Training contains 120 images from one Maldives video from a different BRUVS project; authors still treat Maldives test as a different location. R2 = 복수 (location, campaign/project, species composition: 'only one out of the 10 detected species found in both sets'). R3 = N because in-domain metric (mAP50 on validation) differs from external metric (MaxN Accuracy). C5 from manual verification of 100 random detections per location (FP 86% avg, 95% Caribbean); threshold 0.2 not justified. E5 = same-footage expert MaxN; paper notes expert MaxN was itself wrong in 7% of instances (missed animals), so ground truth was revised with SharkTrack (Table 1 'Number of MaxN Indices Corrected'). PRE not stated (Ultralytics default likely COCO, not coded). Test footage available on request from providers; training data/code on Zenodo (minor subset embargoed). Metadata taken from task brief (S083 not in new_meta.json).
